summary: Elderly man with recently diagnosed widely metastatic adenocarcinoma of unknown primary (brain, bone, lung, liver, adrenal) transferred with chest pressure, fever and refractory hypotension requiring norepinephrine. Echo showed a moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion with RV diastolic collapse/tamponade physiology, treated with pericardiocentesis; concurrent presumed pneumonia was treated. Course complicated by healthcare-associated/aspiration pneumonia, vancomycin-associated acute kidney injury, seizures with fluctuating altered mental status, hypernatremia, anemia and antibiotic/tube-feed diarrhea, ending in transition to inpatient hospice.
most_likely: Malignant pericardial effusion with cardiac tamponade requiring pericardiocentesis

differential.diagnosis: Malignant pericardial effusion with cardiac tamponade
supporting_evidence: Pleuritic chest pressure, hypotension on levophed, pulsus 16
TTE: moderate-large circumferential effusion, RV diastolic collapse
Pericardiocentesis performed; diffuse ST elevations on EKG
Widely metastatic adenocarcinoma with pulmonary/mediastinal disease
opposing_evidence: Fever and RUL opacity raised infection as alternative cause of shock
differential.reasoning: Discharge narrative states he presented with hypotension due to pericardial effusion, with tamponade physiology on echo and therapeutic pericardiocentesis — the condition chiefly responsible for this admission.

differential.diagnosis: Metastatic adenocarcinoma of unknown primary with brain, bone, liver and lung metastases
supporting_evidence: Biopsy-proven metastatic adenocarcinoma, unknown primary
CT head: numerous metastatic lesions with vasogenic edema
Alk phos 879, LDH 344; not chemotherapy candidate, hospice transfer
opposing_evidence: Malignancy known from prior admission, not the acute admitting event
differential.reasoning: The underlying disease driving all complications and the terminal trajectory; a coder may list this as principal for an oncology admission ending in hospice.

differential.diagnosis: Severe sepsis with hypotension due to pneumonia
supporting_evidence: ICU admission for severe sepsis, T 102.6, HR 105, BP 90/47
Norepinephrine required; broad antibiotics (ceftazidime/vanco) given
Bands 8%, neutrophilia 91%, lactate 2.6
opposing_evidence: Initial CXR 'no convincing signs of pneumonia'; lactate 1.7 in ED
differential.reasoning: Septic physiology was the initial working diagnosis and contributed to shock, but pericardial tamponade was the confirmed hemodynamic cause.

supporting_evidence: Two completed courses of HCAP therapy; second felt aspiration-related
CXR: persistent bibasilar consolidations, right pleural effusion
High aspiration risk from altered mental status, Dobhoff feeds
opposing_evidence: Radiology notes opacities could represent atelectasis
differential.reasoning: Explicitly documented and treated with zosyn during this stay; a strong secondary/complication code.

differential.diagnosis: Acute kidney injury, drug-induced (vancomycin) with dehydration
supporting_evidence: Cr rose from 1.0 to peak 2.6, improved to 1.2 at discharge
Vancomycin level 23.7; granular casts 67/lpf in urine
Poor PO intake, treated with IV fluids
differential.reasoning: Clearly documented in-hospital AKI attributed to vancomycin plus hypovolemia; codeable complication.

differential.diagnosis: Symptomatic seizures with encephalopathy due to brain metastases
supporting_evidence: EEG epileptiform discharges left paracentrally; on Keppra, lacosamide, valproate
Waxing/waning mental status, AOx0 at discharge exam
Stable extensive brain metastases with vasogenic edema on imaging
opposing_evidence: No new hemorrhage, infarct or progression on repeat CT/MRI
differential.reasoning: Altered mental status with epileptiform EEG in setting of known brain metastases; multifactorial (toxic-metabolic, infection) contribution possible.

supporting_evidence: Na persistently 147–low 150s; discharge Na 147, Cl 115
Poor PO/water intake, D5W given with minimal improvement
differential.reasoning: Objectively documented electrolyte disorder actively managed during the stay.

differential.diagnosis: Anemia of chronic disease requiring transfusion
supporting_evidence: Hgb fell to 7.0; two units pRBC transfused
Low iron/TIBC, ferritin 2215, normal haptoglobin, guaiac negative
opposing_evidence: Macrocytosis (MCV 103) not typical of anemia of chronic disease
differential.reasoning: Documented workup supports anemia of chronic disease/malignancy rather than bleeding or hemolysis.

differential.diagnosis: Upper extremity venous thrombosis with SVC syndrome status post stenting
supporting_evidence: Ongoing enoxaparin 80 mg BID; swollen upper extremities on exam
Prior R subclavian and extensive left-sided thrombi, patent SVC stent
opposing_evidence: No new imaging of thrombus this admission
differential.reasoning: Chronic active thrombotic disease requiring anticoagulation decisions this stay, but not the acute driver of admission.

rule_outs.why: Chest pressure with EKG ST elevations, but troponins unremarkable and echo showed hyperdynamic LV with pericardial effusion — pericarditis/tamponade pattern.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Acute intracranial hemorrhage or new brain metastasis progression
rule_outs.why: Serial CT/MRI show stable metastases, no new hemorrhage, no midline shift.
Diarrhea attributed to zosyn and tube feeds; no positive testing documented.
